info.bio: T. Rex (originalmente llamada Tyrannosaurus Rex) fue una banda de rock inglesa fundada en Londres en los años 60 que tuvo éxito como grupo de glam rock en los años 70. La banda fue fundada por Marc Bolan en 1967 y tocó sólo una vez como un quinteto en The Roundhouse antes de separarse. Posteriormente quedó reducida a dúo con Marc Bolan y Steve Took, editando tres albumes producidos por Tony Visconti. El sonido era una especie de Folk Rock de una tierra imaginaria, con guitarras acústicas y montones de diferentes y exóticas percusiones.

scenes.name: Decadencia y glam-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El rock siempre tuvo un elemento de decadencia, amoralidad y obscenidad; entre los Cockettes (1968) y el Rocky Horror Picture Show (1974) se convierte en producto de masas. Gran Bretaña lo llama glam-rock: T.Rex lo inaugura y lo casa con el hard rock; David Bowie lo lleva a su cima comercial convirtiendo el marketing en arte (Ziggy Stardust, la trilogía berlinesa con Eno). En EE UU, Alice Cooper, Sparks, Iggy Pop y Lou Reed (Berlin, Metal Machine Music, New York). El glam y la decadencia preparan el punk: Mott The Hoople, Be Bop Deluxe, New York Dolls, Heartbreakers, Dictators, Modern Lovers de Jonathan Richman, Runaways.

podcast.title: Eccentric Persona and Androgynous Style (1970)
podcast.body: Around the release of their self-titled album in 1970, Marc Bolan's public persona grew increasingly eccentric. His behavior and dressing style, featuring an androgynous look with colors and leopard prints, became reminiscent of David Bowie's later 1970s aesthetic. He also shifted from intellectual folk lyrics to more loving, sexually explicit, romantic, and melancholic themes, which became hallmarks of glam music. "Ya fuera de la música, Marvolan se convierte cada vez en una persona más excéntrica."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Reinvention in 1970
podcast.body: In 1970, the band T-Rex underwent a significant reinvention, with Marc Bolan restructuring the group and embracing new sounds. This period saw Bolan incorporating influences from psychedelic music, particularly from eccentric figures like Syd Barrett, whose image and theatrical stage presence inspired Bolan's evolution. "Empieza a correr en 1970, que la banda Tirex prácticamente se reinventa, se reconstruye."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Exceptional Sales and Chart Performance (1971)
podcast.body: Despite having only one Top 10 hit in the US, T. Rex was not a one-hit wonder; in 1971, the band had four number-one singles out of five releases in England. That year, they sold approximately four million records, which surpassed The Beatles' best yearly sales, and sold more 45s (singles) than The Who and Jimi Hendrix combined. "everywhere they went, they tore the place apart."

podcast.title: Glam Rock Catalyst (1971)
podcast.body: In March 1971, T-Rex appeared on the hugely important British TV show "Top of the Pops." During this performance, Marc Bolan, the band's frontman, wore satin clothes and was covered with glitter dust, an event that David Bowie watched at home and found "brilliant," marking it as "the beginning of glam rock" and inspiring Bowie to pursue a similar direction. "In March 1971, T-Rex appeared on top of the pops, the hugely important British TV show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Remembering David Bowie: Part 1

podcast.title: Glam Rock Craze Initiation (1971)
podcast.body: Mark Bolan, at 24 years old, initiated the glam rock craze when T. Rex appeared on Top of the Pops in 1971, showcasing glitter, satin pants, and a sexually heightened, androgynous look. This performance was watched by a nine-year-old David Evans (The Edge) in Dublin, who described Bolan as magical. "Mark Bowlin was magical but also sexually heightened and androgynous with this glitter and makeup."

podcast.title: Musical Influence (Post-1973)
podcast.body: T. Rex was among the musicians whose work Poison Ivy and Lux Interior began to "consume" after being inspired by a New York Dolls concert in 1973. This reflected their growing passion for "anything that was sexy, wild, and played rock and roll." "Esto incluía músicos como al escúper, T-Rex, Ygpop, el acetado New York Dolls."

podcast.title: Mark Bolan's Tragic Death (1977)
podcast.body: Mark Bolan died in a car accident in 1977, leaving his potential future career and his ability to overcome a drug habit as unanswered questions. "Mark Bowlin died in a car accident in 1977."

podcast.title: "Missing Link" in Music Evolution
podcast.body: T-Rex and Marc Bolan are considered the crucial "missing link" that perfectly connects the late 1960s psychedelic music (represented by early Pink Floyd) with the 1970s glam movement. Their albums, especially the three released around 1971, are seen as marking this perfect transition. "Si hay un nombre que conecta lo que es el antes y el después de la música glam de una manera magistral, es Mar Bolancos o banda T-Rex."

podcast.title: Creator of Glam Music
podcast.body: Marc Bolan is widely regarded as one of the great pioneers of glam music, with the assertion that he "possibly the name with a capital letter, who created glam music." "uno de los grandes pioneros en la música glam, a posiblemente el nombre con Magiuscula, que creo la música glam."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Discovery by Tony Visconti
podcast.body: Tony Visconti, a renowned producer, is credited with discovering Marc Bolan. Visconti played a significant role in producing T-Rex's albums during the period he was not working on David Bowie's glam records, thus actively participating in the birth of glam music. "Prácticamente, Tony Biz Conti es la persona que descubra Mar Bolanc."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Early Career - Acoustic Folk
podcast.body: Marc Bolan, with his band T-Rex, began in the late 1960s with a sound far removed from glam music. Their early records were primarily acoustic folk, described as experimental and psychedelic, drawing comparisons to Neil Young, Simon & Garfunkel, and Bob Dylan. This phase had moderate success, likely due to the market's oversaturation with folk music. "Mar Bolanc, con su banda de David Bowie, comienza a finales de los años 60 y sus inicios no tienen nada que ver con la música glam."

podcast.title: Inspiration for Future Rockers
podcast.body: Marc Bolan and T-Rex, particularly through *Electric Warrior*, became a massive inspiration for numerous artists from the late 1970s onwards. He influenced figures like Rod Stewart, Kiss, Def Leppard, and the New York Dolls, making it "very difficult to understand late 70s and 80s rock" artistically and musically without their contribution. "Marvolan como personaje fue la gran inspiración, para gente como rock de estuar, para quís, para deflepar de los New York Dolls."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Later Career and Tragic Death
podcast.body: T-Rex continued releasing glam albums throughout 1972, 1973, and 1975. However, their popularity declined due to Marc Bolan's personal situation and issues within the band. Bolan later recovered and released more successful albums towards the end of his life. Tragically, he died around the age of 30 in a traffic accident, leaving the rock world to wonder what more he could have achieved as a "absolute father of glam music" and a major influence on subsequent rock generations. "Después, Marvolan se recuperaría y hacia el final de su vida sacaría algunos iscos que lo harían resodida. Pero la mala suerte es que cuando tenía más o menos unos 30 años, acababa muriendo por un accidente de tráfico."

xref.title: Fake Live Recording Revelation
xref.body: An alleged live recording of Oasis was revealed by Noel Gallagher in 1997 to be a fake. The actual recording was from a sound check for a Sony convention at the Glen Eagles Hotel in 1993, where the band members were very drunk. They decided to falsely attribute the recording to "Dunning Glasgow" for a cooler image, as the Sony convention was deemed "not cool." The true origin was eventually noted on "The Masterplan" album, and the crowd noise was lifted from a T. Rex bootleg from The Roundhouse around 1973. "It's not from McGee at all. It's actually from a, we got invited to play a Sony convention just before we signed to creation because I think at the time Sony were bankrolling creation and I think they were able to have a look at us."

Bolan's appearance on "Top of the Pops" in March 1971, wearing satin clothes covered with glitter dust, struck Bowie as brilliant and marked the beginning of Glam Rock. "This was the beginning of Glam Rock."

xref.title: Musical Influences and Punk Attitude
xref.body: Oasis's debut album combined new and familiar sounds, incorporating elements of The Beatles, David Bowie, T-Rex, The Jam, The Stones, and The Stone Roses. Their songs were delivered with an intense, almost punk attitude, creating guitar pop as loud as the Sex Pistols but with more groove and melody. "There were bits of Beatles, it's a Bowie and T-Rex and the Jam and the Stones and the Stone Roses in there."
